beats.intro: Chapter six, lesson six. Microtubules, cilia, and flagella. [[swim]]A sperm cell swims. [[lung]]The lining of your airway sweeps mucus upward, all day long. [[split]]And a dividing cell pulls its chromosomes apart. [[map]]Back on our map of the cell, one system lies behind all of this. [[lit]]It is the cytoskeleton. How does it work?
beats.fibres: The cytoskeleton is a network of fibers running through the cytoplasm. [[net]]It organizes the cell's structures and activities, and it anchors many organelles in place. [[three]]There are three kinds of fiber. [[mt]]Microtubules are the thickest, about twenty-five nanometers across. [[if]]Intermediate filaments are in the middle, eight to twelve nanometers. [[mf]]Microfilaments are the thinnest, about seven nanometers. [[roles]]Together they give the cell support and shape, they let it move, and they help regulate its chemistry. [[hook]]This lesson follows the thickest fiber. The other two come in the next lesson.
beats.tracks: A microtubule is a hollow rod. [[tube]]It is about twenty-five nanometers wide, and its hollow center is fifteen. It can be anywhere from two hundred nanometers to twenty-five micrometers long. [[wall]]Its wall is built from thirteen columns of tubulin. [[dimer]]The repeating unit is a tubulin dimer, one alpha tubulin joined to one beta tubulin. [[jobs]]Microtubules shape the cell, guide organelles, and, in cell division, move chromosomes. [[vesicle]]They also work as tracks. A vesicle carries cargo, and a receptor on its surface grips a motor protein. [[walk]]Powered by A T P, the motor protein walks along the microtubule and pulls the vesicle with it. Think of a train on a monorail.
beats.q1: Quick check. Which fiber is which?
beats.centro: Where do microtubules come from? [[nuc]]Near the nucleus, many animal cells have a centrosome. [[moc]]It is a region where microtubules are organized, and from which they grow out into the cell. [[pair]]Inside an animal centrosome is a pair of centrioles. [[ring]]Look at one centriole end on. Its microtubules sit in a ring of nine triplets, three fused tubes in each. [[count]]Nine triplets of three tubes each make twenty-seven microtubules in one centriole. [[div]]Before a cell divides, these are the starting points for the fibers that separate the chromosomes.
beats.cilia: Now back to the sperm and the airway. [[both]]Both are microtubules at work. Cilia and flagella are extensions from the cell, built around a core of microtubules, and covered by the plasma membrane. [[flag]]A flagellum is long. It beats in an undulating wave, like a swimming snake, and the wave pushes the cell forward. [[cil]]A cilium is short, and there are usually many. It beats in two strokes. [[power]]In the power stroke, it sweeps stiffly, and pushes fluid, or the cell, along. [[rec]]In the recovery stroke, it bends back, and returns to start. [[mucus]]Cilia in your airway use this to sweep mucus out of the lungs.
beats.nine: Cut a cilium across, and you see a pattern. [[outer]]Nine outer microtubule doublets, in a ring. [[centre]]Two single microtubules in the center. Biologists call this the nine plus two arrangement. [[spokes]]Radial spokes link each doublet to the center, and cross-linking proteins tie neighboring doublets together. [[base]]At the base, a basal body anchors the cilium to the cell. [[triplet]]The basal body has nine triplets in a ring, and no central pair.
beats.dynein: What makes it bend? [[arms]]Dynein, a motor protein. Dynein arms sit on the outer doublets. [[grab]]Powered by A T P, an arm grabs the neighboring doublet, moves, and lets go. [[slide]]If the doublets could slide freely, they would just slip past each other. [[link]]But the cross-links hold them together, so the sliding is limited. [[bend]]And a limited slide on one side turns into bending of the whole cilium. [[chain]]Dynein movement, limited sliding, bending.
beats.q2: Quick check. What turns the sliding into a bend?
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]The cytoskeleton has three fibers, and microtubules are the thickest. They are hollow tubes of tubulin, and they work as tracks for motor proteins. [[w2]]The centrosome organizes microtubules. In animal cells it holds a pair of centrioles, each with nine triplets. [[w3]]Cilia and flagella have nine doublets and two central microtubules, anchored by a basal body. [[w4]]Dynein slides the doublets, the cross-links limit the sliding, and that makes the bend. [[end]]Now try the practice.
